prize_parts.citation: For establishing the theory, thermochemistry and molecular electrocatalysis of proton-coupled electron transfer

statement.case_for: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the physical mechanism by which respiration, photosynthesis and fuel-forming catalysis move charge. Meyer's early PCET concept and molecular electrocatalysis, Mayer's concerted proton-electron transfer framework and bond free-energy thermochemistry, and Hammes-Schiffer's multistate theory and computation form a quantitative, transferable language that has been confirmed independently in enzymes, molecular catalysts and materials for three decades. It states a fundamental chemical mechanism in physical terms, the criterion I weigh first, and the interpretation is stable, so recognition would be timely rather than premature. Three credited names also fit the cap, with Nocera's work reading more as application and demonstration than founding concept.
statement.case_against: PCET may be judged a field built from separate theory, thermochemistry and catalysis strands rather than one clearly attributable discovery, and I am wary of a candidacy that rests on a line of work. Priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera is not settled by the supplied credit, and Nocera's exclusion would be contested. It also drew only one first-place vote and little wider support in the openings, and I must not mistake my own field proximity for merit. Other candidates, notably B004 and B040, have a sharper single discovery and far wider backing.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig is a general, ligand-controlled, mechanistically understood transformation that is ubiquitous in synthesis, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is only a precursor.
responses.response: I accept the impact and the clean Buchwald-Hartwig attribution, and I see why B004 leads the opening support. My reservation is that the 2010 cross-coupling prize already covers the Pd C-C coupling concept, so the committee must argue that C-N coupling is a distinct achievement rather than a ligand-driven extension. Kosugi's priority also needs the expert report before we omit him. I have kept B004 as my first alternative, but I would want the field evaluation read before it takes the prize.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics is a unified Lagrangian with exactly two authors on the 1985 paper, which makes attribution unambiguous and the citation easy to explain.
responses.response: The attribution argument is strong and I take it seriously, since the three-person cap works against many of the other candidacies. Clear attribution is not the same as the strongest science, however, and my concern is whether the maturity and chemical consequence outweigh the fact that the method's later reach depends on many other groups. I am not persuaded it should outrank a mechanism that explains how biological energy conversion works. I would want the report to show what chemistry it unlocked beyond the original method.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the game-changing delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, with pKa-tuned lipids and rapid-mixing formulation at the core.
responses.response: I agree the impact is unmatched and the pKa-tuning principle is real physical-organic chemistry. My disagreement is attribution. Six credited names across Vancouver, MacLachlan's companies and the Anderson and Langer lipidoid lines cannot be reduced to a defensible three, and the formulation priority questions are partly industrial and patent history. I would not hold the prize back for delivery chemistry unless the reports can identify a clean trio.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation is a genuinely new modality with a design logic of induced proximity, and a three-person prize could span PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues.
responses.response: I share your regard for the mechanistic clarity of cereblon, but I doubt one citation can honestly hold both threads. The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto) and the thalidomide-target discovery (Handa, Ito) are different findings, and Ciulli and Gray are pushed out by the cap. I would ask the reports whether the field is mature as chemistry or still mostly a clinical pipeline.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats PCET as one attributable discovery or as several strands of a field.
Relative priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera, and whether Nocera should displace one of the three.
Whether Kosugi's tin-amide priority and the 2010 cross-coupling prize weaken B004 enough to matter.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the PCET history and have not seen the expert reports in this round.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile. I note that PCET and respiratory proton transfer lie close to my own research field in biological energy conversion, so I will treat that proximity as a bias risk to be checked by the expert reports. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague but is not a candidate.
